The plan is `spud:docs/spikes/bad-036/admin-actions.md` (Charlotte, BADS-036). ## What moves

Two new files under `admin/src/lib/actions/`, exactly as section 4 specifies. Every range below is against BadTakes `main` at `20d11e1`; re-derive them if `main` has moved.

**`support.ts`** — first line `import 'server-only';`, and **no directive**. Moves `Tx` (21-22), `EMAIL_RE` (30), `UUID_RE` (32-36), `normalizeEmail` (38-41), `withOwnedLicense` (377-410) and `message` (412-414); all six become exports. Imports `type postgres from 'postgres'` and `db` from `../db`.

**`auth-admin.ts`** — first line `import 'server-only';`, and **no directive**. Moves `deleteAuthUser` (336-375) and exports it. Imports `secretKey` and `supabaseUrl` from `../env`, `message` from `./support`.

**`actions.ts`** — keeps `'use server'` on line 1 and every one of the twenty actions. Its only edit is to stop declaring the seven moved things and to import them instead (`./actions/support`, `./actions/auth-admin`). The rule comment at 24-28 stays in `actions.ts` in this PR; PR 2 carries it to the barrel. Its exports are still only the twenty async actions, so the intermediate state is legal under the directive.

Why the two support files carry no directive is the whole point of the PR, and section 10 says it plainly: an exported async function in a `'use server'` file becomes a callable POST endpoint. `deleteAuthUser` deletes any Supabase Auth user by email address with the service key and never calls `requireAdmin()`. A directive on `auth-admin.ts` would publish it, and because that file exports one async function and nothing else, the build would not complain. That silence is what the boundary test is for.

## The boundary test

New file `test/server/admin-actions-boundary.test.mjs`, node:test, in the style of the existing `test/server/admin-*.test.mjs` text-assertion tests — read `admin-moderation.test.mjs` and `admin-client-boundary.test.mjs` first and match how they resolve paths and read files.

Section 7 lists four assertions written for the finished tree. Two of them are true today and two only become meaningful in PR 2, so write all four now in a form that is correct at both stages rather than deferring any:

- **(a) Every server action authorises before it mutates.** Over every file under `admin/src/lib/` whose first line is `'use server'` — in this PR that is `actions.ts` and its twenty exports; after PR 2 it is the five leaves — assert each `export async function` opens with `await requireAdmin()`. Write it so it discovers the directive files rather than naming them, so PR 2 needs no edit here. This is the assertion that generalises the moderation test's rule from six actions to all twenty, and it is what catches section 10's worst hazard in either form.
- **(b) The support leaves carry no directive.** `support.ts` and `auth-admin.ts` start with `import 'server-only';` and no `'use server'` anywhere in the file. Discover the non-directive files under `lib/actions/` rather than hard-coding the two names.
- **(c) The barrel.** `lib/actions.ts` contains only comments and `export { … } from './actions/<leaf>'` lines, with no directive. That is **false in this PR and true after PR 2**, so write it as an assertion that recognises both shapes and pins whichever holds — for example, that `actions.ts` is either a directive file whose exports all authorise (covered by (a)) or a directive-free barrel of re-exports, and never something in between. If you cannot make that read cleanly, say so in your Result and leave (c) to PR 2 with a comment in the test file saying why; never write an assertion that passes vacuously.
- **(d) Nothing reaches past the barrel.** No file outside `admin/src/lib/actions/` imports from `@/lib/actions/` or `./actions/`, with `lib/actions.ts` itself the single allowed exception. Note that [[BAD-062]] is the same rule for `lib/accounts/`; do not try to build a shared enforcement here, that ticket is its own.

The test is the one part of this PR that is not a pure move, and the PR body says so in those words.

It is still uncommitted in that worktree because I am not allowed to revert it.
- **A lapsed admin session turns a server action into a dead end** — suggested P3; created as [[BAD-073]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: When the operator's session has expired, submitting a dashboard form does not send them to sign in — the action POST is rewritten to /login by the proxy, the client gets a redirect where it expected an action response, and the page replaces itself with 'This page couldnt load / Reload to try again, or go back'. Reloading then does go to /login, so the recovery exists but the screen does not name it, and the work in the form is gone. For an internal operator tool the honest behaviour is to land on the sign-in form with the destination preserved, which the proxy already computes.
  Evidence: Not diagnosed: why the session lapsed after roughly two minutes rather than at GoTrue's default expiry. That may be local-only and is the part to confirm before treating the timeout itself as a bug — the dead-end rendering is reproducible regardless of why the session ended.
